text:
maria: quick heads-up — ran the cross-device autotune sweep for L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100 on the short/long seq presets this morning. results uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/runs/2026-02-12/1772003456

raj: nice, any standout differences?

dmitri: big one: on short-seq (<=128) L4/T4 prefer the fused rotary softmax kernel we shipped in q4; A100/H100 still best w/ block-8 matmul + nvFused attention. p50 token latency on L4 improved ~18% with fused kernel. :tada:

kevin: ouch, is that stable across batch sizes?

maria: mostly. at batch=1 the fused kernel wins on L4/T4 up to seq=256. above that, its memory layout causes more syncs; A10 behaves oddly — needs the kv-friendly path.

raj: what do you mean by kv-friendly path? any config we should add to presets?

maria: the "kv-preserve" variant: avoid in-place KV compacting and use chunked KV flush. On A10 it reduces copies and keeps Tensor C contiguous, improving throughput for long seqs by ~12%.

perf-bot: autotune job 1772003456 completed. top configs: 
- L4 short-seq: fused-rotary-softmax + small-batch-bypass
- T4 short-seq: fused-rotary-softmax + continuous-batcher=0.75
- A10 long-seq: block-matmul + kv-preserve
- A100/H100 long-seq: block-8 + nvFused-attn + large-batch-aggregation

dmitri: KV cache behavior note: on A100/H100 we can aggressively slice KV into 4MB pages without perf hit; on T4/L4 smaller page sizes (~512KB) are better. this impacts memory fragmentation heuristics in the runtime.

sophia: recorded a perf regression on A10 with latest cuops patch — p95 token latency increased ~9% for seq=1024 under heavy batching. assign to @dmitri?

maria: @dmitri can you repro locally with the failing image? docker: ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:test-cuops-2026-02-11. use the workload harness: `./tools/harness --model redwood-vicuna-13b --seq 1024 --batch 4 --tokens 2000`

dmitri: on it. initial trace shows extra host<->device memcpy at the KV merge point. suspect the cuops change toggled memcpy vs peercopy path. attaching perf snippet: ```
[0.00] launch attention_kv_merge
[0.12] memcpy H2D 1.2ms
[0.40] kernel block_gemm_8x
[0.65] memcpy D2H 0.8ms
```

kevin: if it's memcopies we might be able to change our fallback policy: prefer peercopy when NVLINK present, otherwise compress KV pages into 2 chunks. maybe add that to presets as `peercopy-first` flag.

raj: for rollout plan — propose default presets: `short-latency-optimized` (fused kernels, low batching), `cost-balanced` (A10 kv-preserve + medium batching), `throughput-optimized` (A100/H100 block-8 + large-batch-agg). we should gate `throughput-optimized` behind a capacity check to avoid OOMs.

maria: agree. i'll update the presets json and schedule a canary tomorrow on dedicated pools. also adding a perf regression alert for p95+9% relative to baseline.

perf-bot: canary scheduled: 1772005000 on dedicated-us-east-2 L4 pool. will report after 2 hours. :eyes:
